recent_candidates.title: Dutch court bars BYD vehicle over Range Rover resemblance
recent_candidates.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
recent_candidates.excerpt: BYD’s shares slid Monday after a Dutch court barred European sales of one of its cars over its resemblance to Jaguar Land Rover’s Defender, a significant setback for the Chinese car giant’s Europe expansion plans. BYD’s model isn’t yet for sale in the EU, and Reuters noted it was rare for automakers in Europe to sue over design rights infringement. But the EU is moving to protect its car industry from Chinese competitors who have been aggressively expanding overseas amid a steep downturn at home: Chinese brands took a record 14.5% of Europe’s market in September. But while European automakers may cheer on the Dutch ruling, the so-called “ Temu Range Rover ” has been the UK’s best-selling car for months. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

recent_candidates.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler for $44B in cyber mega-merger
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler for nearly $44 billion in stock , in what could be the largest-ever cybersecurity deal, as demand for their expertise surges on AI hacking fears. The announcement aims to generate synergies between two of cyber’s pure-play titans after a wave of outages at airlines, banks, and government agencies prompted last week’s ouster of the White House cyber director . Experts have ascribed the disruptions mostly to groups using AI to patch numerous preexisting software vulnerabilities, which one expert likened to dead timber: “All that tech that’s on fire [is] going to burn down,” a former National Security Agency official said, clearing the way for new growth. “ But we’ve got to live through this era where stuff’s on fire .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Wall Street rallies on Nvidia CEO Huang's return
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Nvidia’s stock soared more than 30% on Monday — its biggest jump in two decades — after Jensen Huang returned as CEO, providing a boost to US indexes battered by a brutal tech selloff. The chipmaker’s stock had fallen more than 62% from its high of this year following Huang’s exit two weeks ago, which weighed on broader markets, raising fears the AI bubble was bursting . “Huang has become the figurehead of the AI boom and one of the few people who can move the dial on sentiment across the sector,” an analyst said. His comeback signals “ the AI trade is back on ,” an investor said, but other analysts cautioned that scrutiny of Nvidia and lingering concerns about the AI buildout remain. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Commerce adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist
recent_candidates.author: Ashley Gold
recent_candidates.excerpt: The Trump administration on Monday added the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors. The Singapore-based company was added to the Commerce Department’s entity list on Monday afternoon, plans that were first reported by Semafor. The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. According to a filing from Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security posted to the Federal Register Monday afternoon, seven total entities were added to the list from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including various affiliates of Megaspeed, MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. “These additions are being made because of the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users,” the filing reads. “These entities will be added with a license requirement for all items subject to the [Export Administration Regulations] and licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial.” Techno

recent_candidates.excerpt: Some of the Gulf’s largest investors stand to make billions from Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO, a little over a year after CEO Dario Amodei expressed misgivings as he prepared to take the region’s money. In the July 2025 memo, first reported by Wired, Amodei said it would be “ substantially harder ” to stay at the frontier without Gulf capital as the Claude developer fundraised in Abu Dhabi and Doha. recent_candidates.title: The Gulf prepares to face a tougher Democrat-controlled Congress
recent_candidates.author: Lauren Morganbesser
recent_candidates.excerpt: The Democrat-controlled Congress taking power in January could reshape US relations with Gulf partners, bringing greater scrutiny over arms sales, military basing, and technology transfers. Democrats have historically been more critical of Gulf states than Republicans: An analysis by Mahdi Ghuloom of ORF Middle East found that Democrats sponsored 103 of 131 “ negative or critical measures ” targeting the six Gulf states between 2009 and 2026. That scrutiny could intensify, with Democrats using oversight powers to probe the Trump administration’s Gulf ties, particularly over AI exports and technology transfers. Arms sales could face renewed pressure, while Gulf reconstruction after the Iran war may raise questions over funding needed to repair and restart operations on US bases. But translating scrutiny into constraints on the Iran war itself will be harder, given the executive branch’s sweeping foreign policy powers. — Lauren Morganbesser

recent_candidates.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated As Nvidia CEO
recent_candidates.author: Juan David Rojas
recent_candidates.excerpt: The board of chipmaker Nvidia announced on Monday that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as the firm’s CEO. Huang had previously resigned on November 12 after admitting to multiple extramarital affairs with Nvidia employees as well as an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). The Nvidia CEO and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean data center firm Megaspeed, are widely regarded to have illegally smuggled chips to China. American intelligence agencies suspected Alice Huang to have been acting on behalf of Beijing, though doubts have since surfaced as to whether the executive was in fact a Chinese operative. Jensen Huang had previously persuaded President Donald Trump to ease a ban on chip sales to China. Analysts suspect that Huang’s ouster and reinstatement reflects an ongoing dispute between hawks and doves within the Trump administration. Nvidia’s board said it had received input from “senior levels of the United States government” on the decision. The chipmaker’s stock soared by 30 percent on Monday following Huang’s reinstatement as CEO. Since October, Nvidia’s shares had lost nearly half their value amid fears over Huang’s future. recent_candidates.title: Does Coercion Work as a Tool of Statecraft?
recent_candidates.author: John Deni
recent_candidates.excerpt: In September, the United States, Denmark, and Greenland signed an agreement that appears to have defused a crisis generated by Washington. The crisis has been simmering for almost two years, beginning before the 2025 inauguration, when President-elect Trump said the United States needed to “own” Greenland , and that the U.S. could use military force or economic coercion to seize it. Once in office, the president claimed , “One way or the other, we’re going to get it.” For now, though, military force seems unlikely. Instead, the agreement allows the United States to increase its military footprint in Greenland. It also grants U.S. military forces broad access to Greenland and its territorial waters, and it denies base access to any non-NATO country. In sum, although Washington didn’t gain annexation, it looks like the administration’s coercive approach produced a favorable outcome for the United States. Coercion, according to Thomas Schelling , is when one state uses the threat of pain to convince another state to change its course of action. Although coercion can take many forms, this article focuses primarily on economic coercion: specifically, the threatened or actual imposition of sanctions, which has been the Trump administration’s preferred coercive tool. recent_candidates.excerpt: La COP 31 concluyó ayer en Antalya, en Turquía, sin que se alcanzara ningún acuerdo, algo que no ocurría desde la conferencia de Copenhague de 2009 . Las negociaciones debían concluir el viernes 20 de noviembre, pero se prolongaron hasta ayer, 22 de noviembre, lo que convirtió a esta COP en la más larga de la historia. El acuerdo final fue considerado inaceptable por la Unión Europea, las naciones insulares del Pacífico y otros países, ya que no mencionaba explícitamente los combustibles fósiles, principal causa del calentamiento global. Al mismo tiempo, varios países han denunciado la falta de compromisos financieros claros por parte de los países más desarrollados para financiar la adaptación a las consecuencias del aumento de las temperaturas, así como la mención, en el texto del acuerdo, al despliegue de tecnologías de almacenamiento y captura de carbono. El secretario general de la ONU, António Guterres, que dejará su cargo el 31 de diciembre, se ha mostrado «profundamente decepcionado» y ha denunciado lo que ha calificado de «poderosos intereses vinculados a los combustibles fósiles», que, según él, «siguen el manual de los gigantes del tabaco: tergiversar la ciencia, retrasar las políticas, bloquear las medidas y obtener enormes beneficios, mientras que, en todo el mundo, son las poblaciones las que pagan el precio». recent_candidates.title: Hallan restos de las explosiones volcánicas submarinas más profundas conocidas
recent_candidates.author: Sinc
recent_candidates.excerpt: Un equipo internacional liderado por la Universidad de Texas en Dallas (EE UU) ha encontrado rocas de erupciones volcánicas explosivas a más de 6 000 metros de profundidad, junto al Challenger Deep, el punto más hondo del océano. Son las más profundas de este tipo que se conocen, según publican hoy en la revista Frontiers in Earth Science . Los investigadores las localizaron con el robot submarino Jason en una campaña a finales de 2024, en la fosa de las Marianas (Pacífico occidental). Se trata de flujos piroclásticos : fragmentos de magma que una erupción explosiva lanza y que, en este caso, se depositaron en capas sobre el fondo y se soldaron en roca dura cuando aún estaban calientes. Investigadores de la expedición clasifican en el laboratorio del barco las rocas recuperadas por el robot. / Clinton Crowley (UT Dallas) «Sabíamos que procedían de una erupción submarina profunda por la abundancia de fragmentos volcánicos rotos, el vidrio volcánico de la matriz y porque eran rocas bastante resistentes, lo que indica que conservaban calor suficiente para soldarse», explica a SINC Robert J. Stern , geólogo de la Universidad de Texas en Dallas y autor principal del estudio. recent_candidates.title: Irán ve inviable el bloqueo terrestre de EEUU y pide a Washington que negocie un acuerdo

recent_candidates.excerpt: El ministro de Exteriores de Irán , Abbas Araqchi, ha considerado que los planes de Estados Unidos para imponer algún tipo de bloqueo terrestre al país son simplemente absurdos por consideraciones geográficas y por las relaciones diplomáticas que preserva la República Islámica. El Mando Central del Ejército de Estados Unidos (CENTCOM) anunció a principios de mes un plan para bloquear las rutas de suministro terrestres de Irán a través de sus fronteras terrestres y el mar Caspio. Irán comparte frontera con siete países, con Irak en particular (la más larga del mundo, con 1.600 kilómetros), y con Turkmenistán, Pakistán, Afganistán, Azerbaiyán, Turquía y Armenia. Así pues, Araqchi cree que esta iniciativa no tiene ningún sentido porque «un bloqueo terrestre a Irán es prácticamente imposible, ya sea por la extensión del país o por la gran cantidad de provincias» que lo componen, ha explicado a la agencia oficial de noticias iraní IRNA. Trump se «inclina» por reanudar los ataques contra Irán si no hay acuerdo para Año Nuevo THE OBJECTIVE Las provincias fronterizas, en particular, han desarrollado fuertes lazos entre los habitantes al otro lado de las aduanas, con los que comparten raíces históricas y culturales y «poseen la capacidad de abrir lo que el enemigo pretende cerrar» . Araqchi ha pedido así a EEUU que aparque esta clase de planes y se siente a la mesa para negociar un acuerdo racional en lugar de recurrir a herramientas que «ni funcionarán ahora, ni funcionarán jamás».

recent_candidates.author: Lauren Morganbesser
recent_candidates.excerpt: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is planning to travel to the United States in December for the G20 Leaders’ Summit, a US official confirmed to Semafor, a trip that would be his first to the US since the outbreak of the Iran war. The summit, which US President Donald Trump will host on December 14-15 at his Trump National Doral resort in Miami, is expected to bring together leaders from the world’s major economies. MBS’ potential attendance is particularly notable given his limited international travel since the war began. The crown prince also skipped the 2024 and 2025 editions of the summit. If he attends, the gathering could provide an opportunity for Trump and MBS to meet in person for the first time since the outbreak of the conflict. Saudi Arabia has been pressing Washington for assistance in countering Yemen’s Houthis and strengthening the kingdom’s defenses. A face-to-face meeting could provide a forum to discuss those security concerns, particularly given the close relationship between Trump and the Saudi crown prince. The Saudi government did not respond to a request for comment. recent_candidates.title: The UK and EU link their carbon markets
recent_candidates.author: Chloé Farand
recent_candidates.excerpt: The EU and the UK agreed to link their carbon markets in a deal that will reduce trade friction while helping to lower the costs of decarbonization. Since Brexit, Brussels and London have operated similar, but separate, emissions-trading systems that cap industrial emissions and require power plants and factories producing steel, chemicals, and cements to acquire allowances for every ton of carbon they emit. From 2028, allowances will be used interchangeably, creating a larger and more stable market that reduces the risks of investing in clean technology. The agreement also paves the way for mutual exemption of emission-intensive goods from carbon border levies, with the UK’s own carbon tariff coming into force in the new year. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said work would also continue on the UK’s participation in the bloc’s electricity market, which industry groups say would make cross-border trading more efficient and strengthen the case for investments in interconnectors. — Chloé Farand

Depending on your perspective, the failure of negotiators in Türkiye to reach a consensus deal on transitioning away from fossil fuels may not actually be a failure. The UN process worked as designed: The minority of countries that wanted to avoid naming the root causes of climate change were blocked by the majority from pushing through a weak agreement. The compromises needed to achieve consensus in past COPs, the former UK climate advisor Michael Jacobs wrote this week , mainly served to dilute any sense of urgency; failure to reach an agreement is, in this telling, actually a stronger political signal about how deeply committed most countries are to decarbonization. The most obvious solution is to scrap the consensus-driven elements of the COP agenda altogether. In past summits, the topline “cover decision” agreement of the sort that crumbled in Antalya was primarily a kind of thesis statement, framing negotiations on a host of niche tracks, from carbon markets to adaptation finance. recent_candidates.excerpt: The Spirit of the British Constitution: Parliamentary Reform from the Civil War to the Great Reform Act, Max Skjӧnsberg, Princeton University Press, £35 Anyone with a cursory knowledge of English history will be aware of the proposals for political reform advocated by both the Levellers in the 1640s, and then the Chartists in the late 1830s and 1840s, as well as the modest changes actually achieved in between in the form of the ‘Great’ Reform Act of 1832. They will also probably be aware of the writings of Thomas Paine , who advocated sweeping reforms to the institutions of his native country in response to the French Revolution of the 1790s. It is very likely – and much to be regretted – that they will be more or less totally ignorant of the many other politicians, thinkers and movements that proposed a rich and intellectually fascinating variety of reforms to the unreconstructed parliamentary ‘ancien régime’ in the long 18th century. Most of these reformers – ranging from Tory critics of the Whig oligarchy that emerged after 1714, through to the ‘ancient constitutionalist’ reformers who emerged in the 1770s – now languish in obscurity. One suspects that this is because they did not fit smoothly into either the Whiggish or the Marxist frameworks that ruled the roost during the period when English political and constitutional history were still popular subjects of academic research, up until perhaps the 1970s or 1980s. recent_candidates.excerpt: The book of Psalms is full of poetry. This is hardly news. One glance at the book is enough to know these words work differently than Romans and Ephesians. But it’s one thing to know it’s poetry, the book’s “genre” classification; it’s another to consider the nature and purpose of the literature. Why is so much of the Bible written as poetry? Given that Scripture is God-breathed—words from him and of him—why is its urgent and comprehensive message in a form that is concise and understated? These questions are at the heart of my new book, Psalms as Poetry: The Language of Wonder, Prayer, and Praise . I am not a scientist, nor do I know much about computers. But I have been witnessing a slower moving threat which is just as dangerous, albeit not as catastrophically threatening. The idea has a few names, the one I use the most is cognitive atrophy. It’s the idea that if you don’t use your mind in particular ways, your mind will start to shut those areas down. For human beings, our biggest strength is our ability to think. recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: La candidata de Frente Amplio a la Presidencia del Gobierno, Ada Colau , y el alcalde de Badalona y candidato del PP por Barcelona, Xavier García Albiol , han protagonizado este martes un tenso cara a cara en La Sexta, centrado en la crisis de la vivienda y marcado por los constantes reproches sobre sus respectivas trayectorias políticas. En el encuentro, moderado por Ana Pastor a cinco días de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, ambos han confrontado dos modelos opuestos: una mayor intervención del mercado inmobiliario frente al aumento de la oferta y la protección de los propietarios. El dirigente popular ha defendido la necesidad de modificar la Ley del Suelo para facilitar la construcción de nuevas viviendas , mientras que Colau ha apostado por limitar los precios de los alquileres y expropiar inmuebles de los denominados ‘fondos buitre’. La exalcaldesa de Barcelona ha responsabilizado al PP de haber favorecido la especulación inmobiliaria durante los gobiernos de José María Aznar, mientras que Albiol ha reprochado al Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez que la vivienda haya pasado de ocupar el puesto 16 entre las preocupaciones de los españoles en 2018 a convertirse en la principal, según los datos del CIS que ha citado. «El problema no es de los últimos años, se ha cocinado durante décadas y se disparó cuando el PP liberalizó el suelo con Aznar», ha respondido Colau, que ha defendido la necesidad de «desmercantilizar la vivienda y acabar con la especulación». recent_candidates.title: La Policía Nacional intercepta en Ceuta a 50 inmigrantes con el asilo denegado
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: La Policía Nacional ha localizado en las últimas horas a cerca de medio centenar de inmigrantes que habían huido de los recursos temporales habilitados por el Gobierno en Ceuta , después de tener conocimiento de su denegación de la protección internacional. Según han informado a EFE fuentes policiales, la detención se ha producido después de un operativo puesto en marcha por la Policía Nacional en distintas zonas de la ciudad donde se tenía constancia de la presencia de estas personas. Se trata de inmigrantes marroquíes que estaban alojados en distintos centros temporales de la ciudad desde su entrada masiva a finales del mes de julio . Estos inmigrantes habían optado por huir de estos lugares después de tener conocimiento de que se les había denegado el asilo que habían solicitado para permanecer en el territorio nacional. La Policía Nacional ha llevado a cabo esta operación para detener a estos inmigrantes y ser trasladados hasta el CATE de la frontera para ser devueltos a su país de origen. Detenidos dos traficantes de inmigrantes en Ceuta que cobraban 6.500 euros por traslado THE OBJECTIVE El operativo, efectuado por efectivos de la Unidad de Prevención y Reacción (UPR) , se ha centrado en zonas como Hadú, Recinto Sur, Sarchal y Alférez Provisional , entre otras. En todos los casos, estos inmigrantes habían abandonado los centros temporales donde están en régimen abierto para evitar su posible expulsión a Marruecos .

recent_candidates.title: La OMS informa de la primera muerte humana por gripe aviar tras contacto con ganado
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: La Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS, en inglés), informó este martes de la primera muerte en el mundo por el virus de la influenza A(H5) a través del contacto «tras la exposición a ganado lechero infectado o a un entorno contaminado» en Estados Unidos . La OMS ha notificado —en un comunicado— tres infecciones humanas en adultos en el estado de Washington, en el noroeste del país, donde uno resulto mortal. Los tres casos analizados correspondían a adultos que trabajaban en granjas de ganado lechero en el condado de Yakima, «donde recientemente se había detectado el virus de la Influenza Aviar de Alta Patogenicidad (IAAP) —en animales— A(H5N1) en ganado lechero», precisó el escrito. La OMS aseguró que se están llevando a cabo investigaciones y un seguimiento de las personas expuestas, así como de personas cercanas que hayan podido estar cerca a focos del virus, aunque remarcaron que «según la información disponible hasta la fecha, no hay evidencia de transmisión de persona a persona». Los virólogos alertan: «Si la gripe aviar infecta a los humanos, tendremos un problema enorme» Pablo Gallardo «Con base en la información disponible sobre este y casos anteriores, la OMS considera que el riesgo para la población general que representan los virus A(H5N1) es bajo», insistió. Este caso supone la primera muerte reportada en el mundo tras la exposición a ganado lechero infectado. Las autoridades hasta el momento han evitado precisar qué tipo de animal originó el contagio. recent_candidates.excerpt: El chavismo y la oposición venezolana prevén iniciar el quinto ciclo de diálogo el 10 de diciembre para seguir construyendo la hoja de ruta de la reinstitucionalización y la eventual convocatoria a elecciones presidenciales , ha dicho a EFE la jefa de la delegación opositora, Dinorah Figuera. «El 10 de diciembre vamos a estar reencontrándonos nuevamente», señaló tras ser consultada sobre la fecha del inicio del nuevo ciclo.
